label: Shopify store
profile: A direct-to-consumer brand that designs, sources or manufactures a physical product and sells it primarily through its own online store, whether or not it also sells wholesale or on marketplaces.

layers.role: Take payment, host the storefront and manage orders
layers.why: Shopify bundles hosting, a PCI-compliant checkout, abandoned-cart recovery and automatic sales tax into one plan, so a brand selling a physical product can launch without hiring anyone to run a server or patch software.

alternatives.when: When you or an agency already run WordPress comfortably, want zero revenue share, and are ready to own hosting, backups and plugin updates yourselves.

layers.role: Email and SMS marketing that turns one-time buyers into repeat customers
layers.why: Klaviyo's flows read a customer's real order and browsing history from Shopify or WooCommerce, so abandoned-cart, back-in-stock and post-purchase messages run on actual purchase data, and its per-message SMS rate is published rather than something you find out after signing up.

alternatives.when: When your list is still under a few hundred contacts and you want purchase-behavior segmentation included free rather than paying Klaviyo's rates this early.
When you also manage wholesale or outreach accounts and want deal-stage tracking bundled with the same automations that run your consumer email.

layers.role: Hold the SKU list, supplier contacts and SOPs the other two tools were never built to store
layers.why: Notion's free plan has no cap on total storage for a one-person workspace, unlike a free project-management tool's fixed workspace-wide storage limit; the one catch is a 5 MB cap on each individual file, which the paid Plus plan removes with unlimited file uploads.

alternatives.when: When the team is coordinating restock timing, supplier purchase orders and launch dates across several people and needs Gantt or timeline views and workflow automations, not just shared docs.

extras.name: Google Search Console
extras.note: Free. Shows which searches already bring buyers to specific product and collection pages, and flags indexing problems before they cost traffic.

extras.name: Google Merchant Center
extras.note: Free. Lists products in Google's free shopping listings; both Shopify and WooCommerce have an official app that keeps the product feed synced automatically.

extras.name: Google Analytics
extras.note: Free. Breaks down which channels actually bring buyers, in more detail than the ecommerce platform's own built-in reporting.

skip.what: A sales CRM such as HubSpot or GoHighLevel
skip.why: Both are built around a sales pipeline: moving a lead through stages until someone signs. A store selling physical products to consumers doesn't run that process, so the monthly bill buys a workflow this business doesn't have.

skip.what: A second website builder such as Webflow or Squarespace
skip.why: A store's product pages, collections and blog already live on the ecommerce platform. A second site adds a second login, a second bill and a second copy of content to keep current, for a homepage the platform already renders.

skip.what: A dedicated SEO or keyword-research platform
skip.why: Rank-tracking software earns its cost once you're publishing content on a schedule. Before that, a small catalog's search visibility depends far more on complete product titles, descriptions and image alt text than on tracking software.
